intro: Three connectors round off your set of reasons, conditions and contrasts. falls means "if / in case" and is a more careful wenn for a condition that may or may not happen: Falls du Hilfe brauchst, ruf mich an. Nimm einen Schirm mit, falls es regnet (in case — here wenn would not work). da means "as / since" and gives a reason the listener already knows or can accept; it usually opens the sentence: Da heute Feiertag ist, sind die Geschäfte geschlossen. Both falls and da are subordinating conjunctions like weil and obwohl: the verb goes to the end. trotzdem means "nevertheless / anyway" and is the partner of obwohl: the same contrast, but an adverb, so it takes position 1 or sits in the middle and the verb stays second: Es regnete. Trotzdem gingen wir spazieren. = Obwohl es regnete, gingen wir spazieren. Its opposite partner is deshalb (that’s why). The quiz mixes all of them, so read the verb position before you choose.
tips[0].title: falls = if / in case (verb last)
tips[0].text: Falls du Zeit hast, komm vorbei. falls stresses that the condition is uncertain; in most sentences wenn also works. Only falls means "in case": Nimm einen Schirm mit, falls es regnet.
tips[0].check.why: 'In case' is falls, and like weil it sends the verb (wird) to the end.
tips[1].title: da = as / since (verb last), usually first
tips[1].text: Da ich kein Auto habe, fahre ich mit dem Rad. da gives a known reason and is more written than weil. A da-clause normally comes first; the main clause then starts with its verb.
tips[1].trap: German da has nothing to do with English 'there' in this use — and 'since' in the time sense is seit, not da.
tips[1].check.why: da gives a known reason ('as / since'). It sends ist to the end, and the main clause starts with its verb.
tips[2].title: obwohl ↔ trotzdem, weil ↔ deshalb
tips[2].text: obwohl and weil send the verb to the end. trotzdem and deshalb are adverbs: in position 1 they are followed directly by the verb. Obwohl er wenig Geld hat, fährt er in Urlaub. = Er hat wenig Geld. Trotzdem fährt er in Urlaub.
tips[2].trap: 'Trotzdem wir gingen spazieren' copies English word order. After trotzdem the verb comes immediately: Trotzdem gingen wir spazieren.
tips[2].check.why: The verb sind comes straight after the gap, so you need an adverb. trotzdem is the adverb partner of obwohl.
tips[2].visual.rows[0].a: Weil es regnet, bleibe ich hier.
tips[2].visual.rows[0].b: Es regnet, deshalb bleibe ich hier.
tips[2].visual.rows[1].a: Obwohl es regnet, gehe ich raus.
tips[2].visual.rows[1].b: Es regnet, trotzdem gehe ich raus.
tips[3].title: Look at the verb first
tips[3].text: Verb at the end of the gap’s clause → a conjunction (falls, da, weil, obwohl, wenn). Verb right after the gap → an adverb (trotzdem, deshalb). Then choose by meaning.
tips[3].check.why: The verb komme follows the gap directly, so it must be an adverb, and the meaning is 'that's why': deshalb.
remember[0]: falls, da, obwohl, weil: verb last. trotzdem, deshalb: verb second.
mistakes[0].why: trotzdem in position 1 is followed directly by the verb.
mistakes[1].why: After a fronted subordinate clause the main clause starts with the verb.
hook: falls, da and trotzdem let you plan for the unexpected, give reasons and carry on anyway, and each one moves the verb differently.
